reason: CausalBlock.forward applies padding masking only after attention, allowing left-padding keys to absorb attention probability from valid queries. The current macro validation HR@10 of 0.4813 versus baseline 0.505 motivates this controlled correction but does not establish causality. Historical sampled-softmax successes support preserving the objective, while failed retrieval and recency-weighting experiments support avoiding additional architectural or loss changes. Select model_design for the mask correction and training_evaluation to ensure the generated predictor uses identical masking.

plan.model_design: Change only the attention mask in CausalBlock.forward(self, x, mask), preserving its signature, existing variable names, projections, residuals, dropout, and final return x * mask. Derive valid = mask.squeeze(-1).bool() and a lower-triangular causal matrix on x.device; construct allowed query-key pairs as (valid[:, :, None] & valid[:, None, :] & causal) | (~valid[:, :, None] & identity), then expand to shape [b, 1, t, t]. Pass this Boolean allowed mask as attn_mask to F.scaled_dot_product_attention with is_causal=False, remembering that True means allowed for this API; valid queries thereby attend only to nonpadding keys at their own or earlier positions, while padding queries attend only to themselves and are subsequently zeroed. This isolates padding dilution without introducing the learned retrieval or temporal reweighting changes associated with unsuccessful historical experiments. Keep SASRec signatures, dimensions, blocks, heads, embeddings, learned item bias, sampled-softmax objective, NEGATIVES=2048, TOKEN_CAP=2048, token quotas, and endpoint weighting unchanged.
